claims.claim: Microvast links battery-cell/pack manufacturing to commercial and transit electrification, where localized qualified supply can reduce logistics/geopolitical friction and support fleet platforms; Clarksville localization and Huzhou expansion preserve this structural option.

The bottleneck can migrate from capacity availability to utilization: if OEM platform ramps lag, added factories do not create value and instead amplify fixed-cost absorption; substitutes include other qualified battery suppliers and alternative chemistries/platform designs.

factors.name: bottleneckControl
factors.basis: Localized qualified battery capacity can be valuable, but current evidence does not establish scarce contracted utilization.

factors.name: scenarioRobustness
factors.basis: Weak first-half demand and customer delays show capacity economics are sensitive to platform timing and utilization.

factors.name: substitutionResilience
factors.basis: Qualification can create persistence, while competing cell/pack suppliers and chemistry choices remain credible substitutes.

risks.risk: Capacity expansion can become a successor bottleneck if customer ramps do not fill plants fast enough to absorb fixed costs.

causalEdges.mechanism: fleet platforms require qualified cells/packs with reliable regional supply
causalEdges.falsifier: OEM delays persist or competing suppliers/chemistries win the targeted platforms

causalEdges.mechanism: higher utilization can improve fixed-cost absorption and supply responsiveness
causalEdges.falsifier: utilization remains weak and gross margins compress despite added capacity

unknowns.unknown: Contracted utilization and customer mix for incremental Clarksville/Huzhou capacity are not established in cited evidence.

claims.claim: The material present tension is expansion versus absorption: Q2 revenue and first-half revenue weakened while gross margin compressed and capacity investment continued, so the thesis depends on delayed demand converting before added fixed costs impair returns.

Management-cited regulatory/geopolitical dynamics, raw-material inflation and OEM platform delays are external pressures, but they do not remove the company-level requirement to demonstrate utilization and profitable conversion of expansion capital.

factors.name: capacityUtilizationRisk
factors.basis: Weak revenue/utilization while capacity expands can worsen fixed-cost absorption.

factors.name: financingRisk
factors.basis: Expansion requires capital before utilization economics are demonstrated; cited evidence does not quantify a current dilution requirement.

factors.name: confidenceInflation
factors.basis: Installed or planned GWh capacity should not be treated as demand, backlog or earnings without contracted utilization evidence.

risks.risk: Customer-platform delays and low utilization can impair returns on new capacity.
Raw-material inflation and regulatory/geopolitical changes can pressure margins and market access.

causalEdges.mechanism: underutilized assets increase fixed-cost burden and delay cash conversion
causalEdges.falsifier: customer ramps lift utilization and gross margin while new capacity reaches productive scale

contradictions.claim: Long-term capacity expansion thesis coexists with materially weaker first-half revenue and adjusted EBITDA.
contradictions.resolution: Material contradiction remains for Deep Resolver because the cited evidence does not yet demonstrate contracted utilization or timing sufficient to reconcile expansion with current weakness.

unknowns.unknown: Timing, contracted volume and economics of customer ramp recovery remain unresolved.

gatingIssues.defect: Capacity-expansion thesis lacks evidence reconciling incremental capacity with materially weaker first-half demand/utilization.
gatingIssues.nextLawfulEvidencePath: Deep Resolver should adjudicate using customer/OEM ramp evidence, contracted backlog/utilization disclosures, or subsequent primary operating results showing capacity absorption.
